newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian separatist under fire for criticising Pope.
newsitem.headline: Italian separatist under fire for criticising Pope.

text.p: A leading Italian politician who accused the Pope of meddling in politics has come under fire from both government and opposition parties and from the Roman Catholic Church.

Umberto Bossi, leader of the separatist Northern League, said at the weekend the Vatican had taken a step backwards under the leadership of Polish-born John Paul, focusing more on secular matters than on spiritual.
"Bossi's words are the fruit of a personal neurosis: he needs a psychiatrist," said Rocco Buttiglione, head of the Union of Christian Democrats, a centre-right opposition party.
"The Church in Italy does not do politics. Bossi does politics in the most squalid of ways," Buttiglione said in an interview published by La Repubblica on Monday.
Beppe Pisanu, leader of the parliamentary group of opposition Forza Italia deputies, called the remarks "ravings and vulgarities which do not deserve any consideration".
And a spokesman for the Popular Party, which is part of the centre-left governing coalition, said majority and opposition parties should join forces to mobilize against Bossi.
"It makes sense to...join our energies for the benefit of the majority of northern Italians, of the right and of the left, who are tired of Bossi's delirium," Dario Franceschini said.
Bossi clashed with the church last year when he proclaimed independence for the northern "republic of Padania". His latest remarks were made to reporters at his holiday home in northern Italy.

"We're a long way from the times of Pope John XXIII, the great Lombard, who said the Church's interest in politics was finished and it was time for people to busy themselves only with their consciences," he said.
"Since then, the Polish Pope has arrived, has taken the Church and invested it much more with secular powers than with spiritual powers...Under him, the Church has taken a step backwards."
The Roman Catholic daily Avvenire, in a scathing editorial on Sunday, said the remarks showed "an unsurpassed disdain for intelligence".
"Bossi does not represent the people of the Northern League and, above all, does not represent the people of the (northern regions of) Lombardy or Veneto," it said.

The Northern League, which has built its support on frustration with high taxes, central government bureaucracy and the slow pace of reform in Italy, won 3.7 million votes in the last general election.
It polled 30 percent in some northern strongholds, but failed to secure a balance of power in parliament.
Faced with criticism from all sides, Bossi late on Sunday tried to shift the target of his attacks.
"I don't think I so strongly attacked the Pope, maybe the Church. I just told the truth, and in this world of fickle people, the truth is a scandal."
